subject: Proposal: Staggered Warm-Standby Activation & RPO/RTO Liability for GreenWave
messages:
From: Alex Kim <alex.kim@greenwavepay.com>
To: Logan Wright <logan.wright@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Cc: Procurement <procure@greenwavepay.com>
Date: 2028-11-10T09:15:00-08:00
Subject: Multi-region failover SLA — constraints and proposal

Logan / Marissa,

Thanks for the call earlier this morning. Attached is our internal draft SLA (GreenWave_SLA_Draft_v2.pdf) and an activation timing sketch. High-level ask: we need a multi-region failover commitment that supports our payments platform during high-volume windows without risking transactional loss. A few constraints from our side:

- We cannot accept cross-region data loss greater than 2 minutes (RPO <= 2m) for payments processing.
- Our preferred RTO for full traffic cutover is 15 minutes, but we can consider a staged approach if you can guarantee immediate partial failover for critical transactions.
- We need clarity on liability caps if warm-standby activation is delayed due to capacity.

We proposed in the doc a staggered activation: immediate local warm-standby handling critical transactions (tokenized authorization) followed by full cross-region cutover within 30 minutes. Can Redwood outline whether the platform can guarantee per-tenant activation SLAs (e.g., different tiers), and the associated cost delta?

Can you please review and propose a formal carveout or counter-proposal by end of week? Also looping in Procurement (procure@greenwavepay.com) for any contract-level constraints.

Thanks,
Alex
Alex Kim
Head of Platform Reliability
GreenWave Payments

Attachment: GreenWave_SLA_Draft_v2.pdf

From: Logan Wright <logan.wright@redwood.com>
To: Alex Kim <alex.kim@greenwavepay.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.com>
Date: 2028-11-10T13:02:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Multi-region failover SLA — constraints and proposal

Alex — thanks for the clear note and the draft. I reviewed the doc and sketched an activation matrix (attached: activation_matrix.xlsx) that maps traffic tiers to activation windows and expected RTO/RPO behavior. High-level response:

- Platform capabilities: we can support tiered failover commitments. Proposed default tiers for GreenWave: Critical (payments auth & settlement), High (customer-facing flows), Standard (background jobs).
- RPO: for Critical we can deliver 1 minute with KV-cache replication and synchronous commit to a hot-warm cache in the standby region; High/Standard will have longer windows per cost tier.
- RTO: immediate partial failover (Critical) within 5 minutes using traffic steering to warm-standby nodes; full cross-region cutover for the remainder within 30 minutes.

Liability & carveouts: we cannot accept unlimited liability for cross-region network events or operator errors at hyperscale providers. We propose a liability cap linked to the monthly committed spend for Dedicated capacity, with an exception path for customer-provided warm-standby reservations. Kimberly, Marissa — I’ve attached a first pass at the SLA document (GreenWave_SLA_Draft_v2.pdf) incorporating the activation matrix and proposed liability language.

Next steps: if this aligns with you, Kimberly can provide legal redlines and Marissa can quantify estimated cost delta for the Critical-tier guarantees. Happy to set a 30-min session to walk through the activation matrix.

Regards,
Logan Wright
Head of Solutions — Redwood Inference

Attachments: GreenWave_SLA_Draft_v2.pdf; activation_matrix.xlsx

From: Procurement <procure@greenwavepay.com>
To: Logan Wright <logan.wright@redwood.com>, Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.com>
Cc: Alex Kim <alex.kim@greenwavepay.com>, Timothy Chan <tim.chan@greenwavepay.com>
Date: 2028-11-12T10:20:00-08:00
Subject: RE: Multi-region failover SLA — constraints and proposal

Logan / Kimberly,

Thanks for the proposal. A few procurement items to confirm before we proceed to legal redlines:

- Please confirm the uptime % you will guarantee for the Critical tier during our primary region maintenance windows. Our internal target is 99.995% during business hours.
- Provide a clear definition for "immediate partial failover" (what transaction classes are included, and how you ensure sequencing and idempotency across retries).
- We require an SOW-level appendix that lists the expected reserved capacity (GPU counts / instance types) for warm-standby scenarios and the monthly charge delta.

Also, GreenWave has a regulatory requirement to be notified within 5 minutes of any failover activation affecting payments. Can Redwood support the 5-minute notification SLA and provide webhook hooks?

Please attach a cost estimate and the SOW appendix.

Procurement (on behalf of GreenWave)

From: Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.com>
To: Alex Kim <alex.kim@greenwavepay.com>, Procurement <procure@greenwavepay.com>, Logan Wright <logan.wright@redwood.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Date: 2028-11-13T09:45:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Multi-region failover SLA — constraints and proposal

Alex / Procurement team — looping in legal input and redlines. Key legal points and clarifications:

1) Liability cap: Redwood proposes to cap liability for failover-related direct damages to the greater of (i) three times the monthly fee attributable to the committed Dedicated capacity for GreenWave in the prior month, or (ii) $500,000 per incident, with an annual aggregate cap equal to the contract value. We are open to a negotiated uplift if GreenWave is willing to underwrite dedicated warm-standby reservations.

2) RTO/RPO definitions: we will adopt explicit metric definitions in appendix A. RPO for Critical will be defined as the elapsed time between the last successful commit in primary and the last successfully replicated commit available to the standby cluster. For auditability we will provide replication telemetry.

3) Notification SLA: Redwood can provide an automated notification webhook and a 5-minute ops escalation path for declared failovers. We will include a formal notification clause and sample webhook payload in the SOW.

4) Exceptions: network outages outside Redwood's control (cloud provider regional fabric issues, transoceanic link failures) will be treated as force majeure for cross-region delays; however, if Redwood's autoscaling or routing misconfiguration causes delayed activation, we accept the liability framework above.

Attached are our marked redlines: GW_SLA_redlines_kp.docx. Please review; I highlighted the sections where we propose to tie the liability cap to committed spend.

Kimberly Park
Senior Counsel — Redwood Inference

Attachment: GW_SLA_redlines_kp.docx

From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
To: Alex Kim <alex.kim@greenwavepay.com>, Logan Wright <logan.wright@redwood.com>
Cc: Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.com>, Procurement <procure@greenwavepay.com>
Date: 2028-11-15T16:42:00-08:00
Subject: Runbook excerpt + cost delta for Critical-tier guarantees

Alex — following up with operational details. A short runbook excerpt is below and I’ve summarized the expected cost delta for the Critical-tier guarantees. Full runbook and activation playbook will be shared to the Drive link.

Runbook excerpt (high level):
- Detection: platform autoscaling triggers degrade to below Critical threshold OR manual incident declared by Redwood/GreenWave.
- Local warm-standby activation: traffic steering to pre-warmed nodes in the same region; KV cache promoted to read-through mode. Target: <5 minutes for Critical flows.
- Cross-region cutover: DNS/route shift + full instance spin-up in secondary region; target completion 30 minutes for remaining traffic.
- Verification: checksum reconciliation for 1% sample of transactions, idempotency checks for retried payments.

Cost delta (estimate monthly):
- Reserved warm-standby (Critical tier): incremental $38,000/month (N+2 pre-warmed pods, committed GPU reservation).
- Additional replication I/O and telemetry: $2,500/month.
- Optional full active-active footprint for 15m RTO guarantee (no staged cut): estimated incremental $95,000/month.

We can present a cleaned-cost appendix for Procurement and GreenWave finance in tomorrow's 30-min call. Proposed times: Nov 16 10:00-10:30 PT or Nov 17 14:00-14:30 PT.

Marissa Cole
Director — Platform Operations, Redwood Inference

From: Alex Kim <alex.kim@greenwavepay.com>
To: Logan Wright <logan.wright@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Cc: Procurement <procure@greenwavepay.com>, Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.com>, Timothy Chan <tim.chan@greenwavepay.com>
Date: 2028-11-15T17:05:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Proposal: Staggered Warm-Standby Activation & RPO/RTO Liability for GreenWave

Thanks everyone — that level of detail is really helpful. GreenWave is prepared to move forward with the staged model as a starting point. A few quick notes before legal finalizes redlines:

- We accept the proposed liability cap tying to committed spend, subject to a short-term uplift if we commit to the reserved warm-standby numbers Marissa outlined.
- Please include the 5-minute notification webhook and the 1-minute RPO guarantee for Critical tier explicitly in appendix A.
- We’ll review Kimberly’s redlines and get back with any narrow asks by EOD Monday.

Please schedule the ops walkthrough for Nov 16 10:00 PT; Tim will join from GreenWave.

Appreciate the quick turnaround — Alex

Alex Kim
Head of Platform Reliability
GreenWave Payments
